land.text: Kufa and most of Iraq, with the Jibal and Azerbaijan

predecessors.note: Mukhtar drove out the Zubayrid governor of Kufa in October 685 (Second Fitna page).

land.text: Kufa, Iraq and the Jibal and Azerbaijan

successors.note: Mus'ab, Zubayrid governor of Basra, took Kufa on 3 April 687 (Mukhtar page).

capitals.name: Kufa
capitals.note: His palace at Kufa was where he held out for four months and died.

rulers.name: Mukhtar al-Thaqafi
rulers.title: leader of the Kaysanites, avenger of Husayn
rulers.note: Ruled 'for eighteen months'; declared Ibn al-Hanafiyya the Mahdi (undated).

correction.text: 685-687: Iraq without Basra, with north-western Iran

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mukhtarid row; it gives the Umayyads Iraq in 682-691). After taking Kufa Mukhtar 'controlled most of Iraq and its dependencies including Arminiya', plus Azerbaijan, the Jibal and parts of the Jazira; the Second Fitna page says 'most of Iraq and parts of north-western Iran'. The shape is Iraq without Basra, which stayed Zubayrid, plus Media and Iranian Azerbaijan. Arminiya and the Jazira are left out because the page names them without an extent.

region.text: north-western Iran: Azerbaijan and the Jibal

ledger.note: Page silent on when. Mukhtar page: his dominions included 'Azerbaijan, Jibal (northwestern Iran)' and 'parts of the Jazira'; the Second Fitna page says 'parts of north-western Iran'. Placed with the taking of Kufa (685) as the earliest date. The extent is unknown: the shape is Media (the Jibal) with Iranian Azerbaijan, a generous reading of 'parts'. Arminiya, named as a dependency, and the Jazira are left out of the shape. Re-read on the Mukhtar page (2026-10-19): the sentence 'At this stage he controlled most of Iraq and its dependencies including Arminiya, Adharbayjan, Jibal and parts of the Jazira' follows Ayn al-Warda (January 685) and precedes the Mosul fight of July 686 and Khazir (early August 686), so his authority reached them between October 685 and July 686; the page gives no month, and names no governor of Azerbaijan, Media, Hamadan, Rayy or Isfahan. 685 stays a bridging. Mirror: zubayrid-caliphate /ledger (685 loss of the Jibal and Azerbaijan).

region.text: Kufa, seized from the Zubayrid garrison

ledger.note: 18-19 Oct 685: Mukhtar page: the plan to seize Kufa was fixed for 'Thursday, 19 October 685'; his forces defeated the Zubayrid garrison on 18 October and Kufa gave him its allegiance the next morning. The Second Fitna page: in October 685 he 'overthrew the Zubayrid governor and seized Kufa'. He was hostile to Ibn al-Zubayr.

region.text: most of Iraq (Basra stayed with Mus'ab)

ledger.note: Oct 685 on: Second Fitna page: Mukhtar held 'most of Iraq and parts of north-western Iran'; the Mukhtar page: after taking Kufa he 'controlled most of Iraq and its dependencies including Arminiya' and gave Mosul and al-Mada'in to Arab governors. The page dates no step after Kufa; the rest of Iraq is placed with the taking of Kufa. Basra is left out because Mus'ab was the Zubayrid governor there when he moved against Mukhtar.

region.text: Mosul and the Jazira front, where Mukhtar's cavalry met the Umayyad army

ledger.note: 17 Jul 686: Mukhtar page: Mukhtar's cavalry 'defeated an Umayyad army near Mosul' on 17 July 686, which opens the war with the Umayyads under Ibn Ziyad.

Aug 686: Khazir. Mukhtar page: 'early August 686' (some sources 6 August) the Umayyad army was defeated and Ibn Ziyad killed; the Second Fitna page dates Khazir August 686. 'Abd al-Malik reconquered Iraq after the Battle of Maskin' in October 691 (Second Fitna page).

region.text: Kufa and its approaches, attacked by Mus'ab

ledger.note: 687: Mukhtar page: Mus'ab attacked Kufa, defeated the Kufans at Madhar and Harura, 'then besieged Mukhtar's palace for four months'. The page gives the year and the four months, not the month of the first attack.

region.text: Kufa and Iraq (Basra was Zubayrid), with the Jibal and Azerbaijan, taken by Mus'ab

ledger.note: 3 Apr 687: Mukhtar page: 'On 3 April 687 Mukhtar came out of the palace with nineteen supporters' and was killed in Kufa; Mus'ab took the palace (Second Fitna page: killed April 687). Region widened to the whole of the 685-687 keyframe (review of 2026-10-19): the Jibal and Azerbaijan pass back to the Zubayrids with Kufa (confidence 1: the Mukhtar page does not say who held them after April 687).
3 Apr 687: the siege of Mukhtar's palace ends with his death (Mukhtar page). The Kufa zone is the fighting; the north-west goes with the loss above.

region.text: Kufa and the lands that depended on it, the whole of the regime

ledger.note: 3 Apr 687: Mukhtar dead, 'ruled for eighteen months' (Mukhtar page); his followers are called the Kaysanites. The land handed on is the whole keyframe, as the zubayrid-caliphate dossier gains it in April 687.

wars.name: Second Fitna

zones.text: Kufa, taken and lost by Mukhtar (685-687)
Mosul and the Khazir front, July-August 686

wars.outcome: Umayyad victory in the war as a whole; Mukhtar's regime was crushed by the Zubayrid governor of Basra on 3 April 687.
wars.note: Mukhtar page: Khazir early August 686, the siege of the palace lasted four months and ended with his death on 3 April 687.

certainty.note: The pages give a list of provinces under his governors, not borders; north-western Iran, Arminiya and the Jazira are unlocated.

sources.title: Mukhtar al-Thaqafi
sources.note: Kufa 18-19 Oct 685, Mosul and Khazir July-August 686, death 3 April 687, the extent of his rule.

sources.title: Second Fitna
sources.note: Zubayrid loss of Kufa in October 685; 'most of Iraq and parts of north-western Iran'.

notes:
Written for group me-07 on 2026-10-19 from two pages. State Cliopatria lacks. The Kaysanite movement (Mukhtar declared Ibn al-Hanafiyya the Mahdi) is not treated. Not on the pages: when Azerbaijan, the Jibal, Arminiya and the Jazira came under his governors, where Mosul and al-Mada'in sat in the lines, whether Basra was ever contested. The Umayyad dossier of this group has no Mukhtarid events (the Khazir war is in its Second Fitna entry).
Repair of 2026-10-19 (review me-07): the 687 loss, the dissolve and the successor land now cover the whole 685-687 keyframe (Iraq without Basra, Media, Iranian Azerbaijan), not Iraq alone, and the Zubayrid dossier mirrors both the 685 loss and the 687 regain. The Mukhtar page also names Arminiya and parts of the Jazira among his dependencies; neither is drawn (Arminiya is conquered from Byzantium in 692; the Mosul fight of 686 is a contest zone).
